What Environment Means To Me Our Non Human Neighbours

Aug 1, 2016 • Janice Cotcher

Part of taking care of my loved ones is the also taking care of my non-human neighbours. People are often willing to campaign to save animals if they are cute and cuddly. We often forget that our precious Eco-system has creepy, crawly, and dangerous creatures that vital to keeping this system in balance. In addition, part of saving animals is preserving their habitats.

A modern problem that can harm to animals in the wild is the release of unwanted pets. People think they are being kind by releasing an unwanted rabbit or fish in to the wild. these domesticated animals are not part of the Eco-system and may not have any natural predators.

In the case of Victoria, BC (pictured below), the university became overrun by bunnies. They burrowed under buildings and in fields until it became a serious safety hazard. Citizens wanted the rabbits to be adopted rather than to be culled. Due to the rate of reproduction of the bunnies (as they are known to do) and having no predators, culling was the only solution.
